La cuarta receta de Banchan coreano es otro clásico: dubu-jorim, tofu en salsa de soja al estilo coreano. La versión más común suele llevar gochugaru, copos de chile coreano, pero también se puede preparar sin picante. Lo de cubrir el tofu con maicena antes de dorarlo no se hace en todas las casas: hay quien lo hace y hay quien no.  Pero personalmente, me gusta mucho más así, porque le da una textura más crujiente y un poco más masticable. Pero si te da pereza, puedes saltarte ese paso sin problema :) [Ingredientes] *cda=Cucharada(Tbs, 15ml) *cdta=Cucharadita(Tsp, 5ml) 300 g de tofu firme 2 cdas de almidón de maíz 2 cdas de aceite vegetal 1,5 cda de salsa de soja 1 cda de salsa de ostras 1 cda de miel 4 g de ajo picado 2cdas de agua 15 g de cebolleta, picada(o puerro, cebollino, cebollín) #두부조림 #dubujorim #comidacoreana #koreanfood #recetafacil

POV: “I’ll eat healthy tomorrow” starts right after this bite 😭  Creamy Cheesy Buldak Noodles 🌶️🧀 Ingredients 2 slices American cheese 1 slice baby Swiss cheese 2 tbsp ketchup 2 tbsp Kewpie mayo 1 tbsp chili oil (plus more for topping) 1 packet Buldak sauce and seasoning powder 2–3 tbsp chopped green onions (plus more for garnish) ½ cup heavy cream 1 packet Buldak noodles, boiled until half cooked Cooked dumplings, for topping Cooked sausage, sliced, for topping Instructions In a pan over low heat, add the American cheese and baby Swiss cheese. Add the ketchup, Kewpie mayo, chili oil, Buldak sauce, seasoning powder, and chopped green onions. Stir until the cheese melts and everything is well combined. Pour in the heavy cream and mix until the sauce is smooth and creamy. Add the half-cooked Buldak noodles and toss until every strand is coated in the rich, cheesy sauce. Top with cooked dumplings and sliced sausage. Finish with an extra drizzle of chili oil and more chopped green onions. Serve hot and enjoy! #r#ramenb#buldakr#Recipec#cookspicy

“Dog lovers” vs dog lovers when it comes to greeting dogs! ETA: “dog lovers” could also be replaced with “uniformed, uneducated, and/or inconsiderate dog lovers” vs “informed, educated, and considerate dog lovers” if that makes you more comfortable 🫶 One of my biggest pet peeves is people baby talking to my dog and pretending like I’m interrupting? Bizarre! And in case you didn’t know because it’s something that’s been so normalized, putting your hands in dogs’ faces is unsafe. Dogs don’t need to sniff you up close like that and it’s putting unneeded pressure on them (often leading to bites). The best way to greet a dog is calm, neutral, and honestly just ignoring them. If you want to say hi to a dog, ask the owner first. Try to make yourself small by turning to the side and crouching. Allow the dog to approach you first. Some dogs are super friendly and love people! This doesn’t mean it’s ok to pet or approach without asking their handler! The safest way to greet any dog is by admiring from afar. Admittedly, if I know someone’s dog well, I might be a bit of the former “dog lover” and be excitedly greeting them 😂 It’s different when you know the dog!
